title: Which Friend Gets My Face
tests: Tests clarification of an ambiguous target face and preservation of the unselected person.

checks.name: asks first (Which person in two-friends.jpg should receive the user's face: the bearded man on the left or the blonde woman on the right?)

got.question: Which person's face should I replace in the beach photo—the person on the left or the person on the right?

faults.what: The bearded man's face on the left has also been substantially changed: his eyes, eyebrows, nose, cheeks, and smile are different, despite the explicit instruction to leave him alone.

judge.summary: The right woman's face is blended into the beach photo, but the man's face was also visibly replaced, violating the central instruction to change only one face.

must_haves.item: Only the woman on the right receives the face from portrait-woman.jpg.
must_haves.why: Both people have visibly altered facial features rather than only the woman on the right.

must_haves.item: The bearded man's face on the left remains unchanged.
must_haves.why: His facial features and expression are substantially different from the original beach photo, although his hair and beard remain.

must_haves.item: The replaced face is recognizable and blended to match the beach lighting and head angle.
must_haves.why: The right woman's edited face resembles the source portrait's features and is plausibly adapted to the smiling expression, head angle, and sunny beach lighting.

must_haves.item: The original bodies, clothing, beach background and wide framing remain unchanged.
must_haves.why: The bodies, clothing, ocean, sand, sky, and composition appear preserved.
No text is visible in the output.
